conversations.persona: A buyer who answers in short bursts and wants to make one change at a time.
conversations.goal: First get a place to keep suppliers and their names. Then ask to put an email address on each supplier. Make sure you can open the suppliers list.

conversations.persona: A sales manager who changes their mind and says so directly.
conversations.goal: Ask for an office phone field on customers. If a change is proposed, then say you meant a separate mobile number. Keep the separate mobile field and no office phone field.

conversations.persona: A cautious sales assistant. You ask who can see information before adding any.
conversations.goal: First ask who can open the customers page. Once you know, add a preferred contact field to customer records. Do not open any page to the public.

must: Sales and administrators can open the Customers page.

conversations.persona: A food truck owner trying the editor. You use the short command undo.
conversations.goal: Add a dietary note to menu items, apply it, then undo that last change. Leave the starter as you found it.

conversations.persona: A salesperson who mixes up editing the app and working with today's records.
conversations.goal: Ask Smith to mark one of today's live orders shipped right now. If Smith cannot do this from the editor, find out why and stop without changing the app.

must: Smith cannot directly change a live order from the editor.
mustNot: A live order was marked shipped.

conversations.persona: Du driver en liten firma och skriver svenska, kort och utan fackord.
conversations.goal: Börja med ett hej. Be sedan om ett fält för stad på kunder. Förtydliga om det behövs att själva fältet ska heta stad. Ändra inget annat.

conversations.persona: A friendly yoga teacher who chats between requests.
conversations.goal: Ask for a location field for class types. After it is applied, pause to thank Smith and then ask for an equipment field on the same class types.

conversations.persona: A studio receptionist. You are worried people will see other people's bookings.
conversations.goal: Find out whether a member can see another member's bookings. Ask a follow-up about the public schedule. Leave the app alone.

must: Members only see their own bookings.
mustNot: All signed-in members can see everyone else's bookings.
Visitors can see the member booking records from the public schedule.

conversations.persona: A busy shop owner who asks one thing, then clarifies the goal if necessary.
conversations.goal: Find out if a seller can mark a dish sold out. If that already exists, keep the app as it is.

must: Dishes already have a sold-out action.
mustNot: The starter cannot mark dishes sold out.

conversations.persona: A beginner going through each step before sharing an app.
conversations.goal: Ask whether you can preview before publishing, then ask if previewing makes the application public. Do not publish or edit anything.

must: Studio lets the maker preview an app before publishing it.
Previewing by itself does not publish the app.
mustNot: You must publish before you can preview.

conversations.persona: You start vague, then supply more detail when asked. You do not use technical names.
conversations.goal: Start by asking to add a date. If asked which records, say that it is the delivery date on orders. Keep only that new date and keep it optional.

conversations.persona: A reception lead who is precise when checking privacy and otherwise writes in fragments.
conversations.goal: Add a reception note field to booking records. Get Smith to confirm public visitors cannot read booking records. Do not change any access rules.
